content.intro: This lesson covers Appending Queries as part of Power Query and Data Preparation. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Appending Queries supports repeatable analysis by organizing, cleaning, summarizing, or relating data. Preserve the raw source and reconcile a summary back to its input records. Compatibility: Power Query, the Data Model, Power Pivot and DAX are related but distinct capabilities; their exact availability varies by Excel edition, operating system, license and update channel. Follow the course’s local availability checklist before building a dependent workflow.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Appending Queries focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Combining datasets vertically; Matching column structures; Combining monthly or regional files; Handling schema differences. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: A Power Query M transformation changes OrderDate to date and Amount to currency types, assuming these source column names exist.
content_blocks.run_instructions: In Excel, use Data → Get Data to open Power Query Editor; replace Source with the actual prior step and verify locale-sensitive dates and currency values before loading.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates appending queries. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
